poems.title: The Lamb
poems.author: William Blake
poem_stanzas:
Little Lamb who made thee
Dost thou know who made thee
Gave thee life & bid thee feed.
By the stream & o'er the mead;
Gave thee clothing of delight,
Softest clothing woolly bright;
Gave thee such a tender voice,
Making all the vales rejoice!
Little Lamb who made thee
Dost thou know who made thee

Little Lamb I'll tell thee,
Little Lamb I'll tell thee!
He is called by thy name,
For he calls himself a Lamb:
He is meek & he is mild,
He became a little child:
I a child & thou a lamb,
We are called by his name.
Little Lamb God bless thee.
Little Lamb God bless thee.

missing_words.definition: A meadow; grassy lowland, often near water.
missing_words.rhyme_hint: Rhymes with 'feed'; where the lamb feeds by the stream.

missing_words.definition: Covered with soft, thick hair like a sheep's fleece.
missing_words.rhyme_hint: Describes the soft clothing of delight, bright to the eye.

missing_words.definition: To feel or show great joy and gladness.
missing_words.rhyme_hint: Rhymes with 'voice'; what the vales do at the tender sound.
